children: Japan is set to stop short of explicitly adopting a defence spending target of 3.5% of GDP in a planned revision of its national security strategy later this year, despite repeated US calls on allies to meet that benchmark, the Asahi newspaper reported on Friday.

The government is instead leaning toward significantly increasing defence-related spending over the next five years, including broader security expenditures, the report said, citing multiple government sources.
Tokyo hopes that a demonstrated commitment to strengthening military capabilities will appease Washington, the report added.
The defence ministry did not immediately respond to an emailed request for comment on the report.

According to Asahi, US President Donald Trump's administration has repeatedly urged Japan behind closed doors to raise defence spending to 3.5% of GDP, describing the level as a global standard for allies.

But formally committing to such a target would pose a major fiscal challenge for Tokyo. Defence spending at 3.5% of GDP would exceed 20 trillion yen ($126.52 billion) annually, requiring substantial new funding sources and likely forcing politically sensitive tax increases, Asahi said.
